Use case: illustration-story.
Asset: a square 1:1, hand-painted watercolor narrative illustration for an adult visual book, warm, thoughtful and lightly humorous. Create a complete new image from this description. The story shows a paid carpenter choosing responsibility for his work after the payment is already complete.

COMPOSITION AND READING ORDER
Three connected comic scenes within one square: two equally sized upper panels separated by a narrow clean white vertical gutter, and one wide lower panel across the full width. Read the upper RIGHT first, upper LEFT second, and LOWER scene last. The upper scenes together occupy approximately the upper half; the final scene occupies approximately the lower half. Use thin white gaps, no heavy black panel frames. Each scene has softly irregular watercolor endings, and clean white paper remains around all outer edges. Set the view wide enough to include every complete character, both feet or kneeling feet, the chair, table legs and all essential tools. Nothing is cut by a panel edge. Objects may naturally overlap, but torso-to-leg connections must remain physically continuous.

CONSISTENT CAST
The same PURPLE adult carpenter appears in all three scenes. The same LIGHT GRAY adult customer appears in the upper-right and lower scenes. They have identical medium, balanced, neutral adult builds: gently near-parallel torso sides, moderately sized arms, natural legs, neither thin and stretched nor round/chubby, no childlike or chibi proportions. No breasts, narrowed waist, protruding hips or buttocks, body indentations or gendered silhouette. No hair, ears, noses or necks. Heads are genuinely PERFECT CIRCLES with equal width and height, without a jaw, chin, oval shape or flattened lower edge, joining shoulders directly. A soft crescent of darker local watercolor under the head distinguishes it from the torso. Purple wears the SAME simple straight CREAM work apron in every appearance: shoulder straps, unwaisted rectangular bib and skirt, a small work pocket containing a pencil/ruler or small tool, and a modest tie. Gray has a plain gray body. No other clothing or shoes; feet are the same body color.
Faces have modest dark oval eyes with optional tiny white glints INSIDE the dark eye, simple eyebrows and minimal mouths; no surrounding white sclera. The customer's happy upper-right eyes are small closed upward arcs; the lower customer's eyes are open dark ovals. Do not add eyelashes to either character. Purple's face changes from pleased attention to payment, to thoughtful concern, to a calm responsible smile. Each anatomically complete hand has THREE fingers and ONE thumb; use simple natural grips without extra digits, allowing normal object occlusion.

UPPER RIGHT: PAYMENT AND DELIVERY
A modest warm wooden carpentry workshop doorway. Gray stands on the LEFT and holds the repaired small wooden chair; purple stands on the RIGHT, smiling eagerly and receiving a small cream payment envelope. The envelope clearly reads exactly "دستمزد". Purple's attention is on the payment. Gray is pleased and unaware of any problem. The chair is recognizable honey-brown wood with a simple solid backrest, flat seat, four legs and a horizontal brace beneath the seat. On the near-side horizontal brace joint is one clearly EMPTY dark screw hole, with two small unobtrusive emphasis strokes below it. The chair has not collapsed and nobody is hurt. Keep the chair complete and its perspective coherent.
The workshop background contains a few hanging hand tools, upright wooden boards, a small overhead warm lamp, a pale stone/tile floor and one modest green potted plant. A small hanging wooden shop sign at upper right reads exactly "نجاری". Keep both standing figures and their two feet fully visible inside this panel.

UPPER LEFT: THE MISSED SCREW
Later, the SAME purple carpenter stands alone behind a wooden workbench, wearing the same cream apron. His entire neutral body and both feet are visible beneath the tabletop; the bench's legs frame rather than hide both feet. In his hand on the image-right he holds ONE small distinctive brass screw. His other hand rests thoughtfully near his chin, with worried brows: he has realized the screw was left out. A closed payment envelope already lies at the left of the bench and again reads exactly "دستمزد". A black-shaft screwdriver with a red handle lies horizontally on the bench at image-right. Spare boards, a small tool holder and hanging workshop tools stay in the restrained warm background.
A white thought bubble above him, connected by small thought circles, contains a close-up of the wooden chair's brace meeting a leg and its EMPTY screw hole. It also contains the exact short Persian thought "این پیچ جا مونده!", comfortably arranged on two lines. This inset is a thought image, not a second real chair in the workshop. The brass screw and the matching empty joint make the discovery understandable at a glance.

LOWER WIDE SCENE: RESPONSIBILITY AFTER PAYMENT
At the gray customer's warm, simple home doorway, gray stands full-bodied on the LEFT, surprised kindly, with hands raised near his chest. The SAME wooden chair stands fully visible near center. Purple is to its RIGHT, kneeling naturally with continuous torso, hips, bent legs and complete feet, still in the same cream apron. He calmly uses the red-handled screwdriver to place the brass screw into the EXACT near-side horizontal-brace joint that was empty in the first scene. His other hand steadies the chair. The customer had not complained or discovered the fault; the carpenter has returned voluntarily. No additional money is exchanged.
Gray's speech bubble at upper-left of this scene, with a clear tail to gray, says exactly "ولی پولت رو گرفته بودی!", arranged on two readable lines. Purple's white speech bubble at upper-right, with a clear tail to purple, says exactly "کارم باید درست باشه.", arranged on two lines. Their expressions convey genuine surprise and quiet responsibility, without grandstanding. The setting has a pale peach wall, warm wooden doorframe at left, a simple patterned rug beneath the figures and chair, and a small cabinet, modest framed landscape and leafy potted plant at right. All bodies, feet, chair legs and screwdriver fit inside the scene.

WATERCOLOR AND FINISH
Authentic moderate hand-painted watercolor on visibly textured warm white paper. Show broad irregular overlapping translucent washes INSIDE heads, torsos, arms, legs and hands as well as backgrounds; luminous lighter patches, gently varied pigment density, soft natural bleeding and subtle pooling near some edges. Soft painted highlights, never glossy 3D shading. The character contours are darker versions of each character's OWN body color: deep purple around purple and slate gray around gray, never black body outlines. Keep cheeks within their own local translucent body wash: no sharp pink round spots or sticker-like blush. Wood is built from warm transparent washes and modest grain; backgrounds are purposeful and subordinate to faces, screw and chair. Maintain bright, gentle book illustration warmth without excessive decoration, heavy mottling, flat vector fills, marker strokes or uniform colored-pencil grain.

TEXT AND LIMITS
All in-image writing is ONLY the five exact connected Persian strings quoted above: "نجاری", "دستمزد", "این پیچ جا مونده!", "ولی پولت رو گرفته بودی!", and "کارم باید درست باشه." The payment label may appear on the two envelopes as described. Use correct joined right-to-left Persian, dark legible lettering and clear bubble tails. Do not place the English book sentence in the image. No extra captions, moral slogans, English, numbers, logos or watermarks. No injuries, broken chair accident, new reward, money pile, trophy, extra people or new narrative event. Keep the causal sequence clear: payment received, omitted screw recognized, voluntary repair after payment.

ideas.fullGenerationPromptEnglish:
Create one finished square, 1:1 narrative watercolor illustration for a thoughtful visual book for adults and teenagers. Arrange THREE broad horizontal scenes stacked from top to bottom, with slender clean white gutters and no heavy comic frames. The story is an artist changing from seeking personal recognition to acknowledging a coworker's contribution during the actual work. Make the same courtyard and the progress of the same wall mural recognizable across all three scenes. Use only TWO characters: a GREEN adult artist on the left and a CORAL adult artist on the right. Their colors, builds, faces and matching cream work aprons remain consistent. The narrative must be immediately understandable through the actions, shared artwork and authorship cards; do not add an explanation of the book's advice to the picture.

PAINTING MEDIUM AND BOOK STYLE
Paint a genuine, moderately textured hand-painted watercolor on white watercolor paper. Use luminous overlapping translucent washes, broad varied strokes and gentle pigment pooling at a few natural edges. This layered watercolor must visibly exist INSIDE the characters' heads, torsos, arms, legs and hands, as well as in the mural, masonry and paving. Leave some lighter paper showing through the paint. Avoid smooth flat fills, vector shapes, marker shading, colored-pencil grain, plastic gloss, airbrushed 3D surfaces and exaggerated stains. Define the green character with restrained darker green contours and the coral character with darker coral or burgundy contours, never black outlines around their bodies. Faces use small dark facial marks. Ground the people with quiet watercolor contact shadows under their feet. The outer painted edges are organic and irregular, with clean white paper around all four sides. Keep every body, both feet, brush, bucket, sign and the entire tripod within its own scene with breathing room. The top and middle must be fully framed, rather than showing cropped bodies above a gutter.

CHARACTER DESIGN
These are stylized adult book characters with medium, balanced, neutral bodies. Their torsos are simple and almost straight sided; their arms are modest in width, their legs have believable adult length, and their rounded feet are planted naturally. They are neither skinny nor swollen, and they are not babies, chibi figures or toys. Every head is a true CIRCLE of equal width and height, with no oval extension, pointed chin, jaw, ears, nose, hair or separate neck. The head joins the shoulders directly; show a soft darker local-color crescent contact shadow beneath the round head so its boundary is visible. Gender never changes the silhouette: no breasts, pinched waist, accentuated hips or buttocks, bulges or indentations. Green can have a few fine SHORT upper-outer eyelashes attached to the SAME small dark oval eyes as the other character. Do not enlarge the eyes or turn them into a different eye style. Tiny white glints may occur INSIDE the dark eyes; there is no surrounding white sclera. Closed happy arc eyes are appropriate for coral in the last scene. Use small expressive eyebrows and a friendly curved mouth, occasionally a small open happy mouth. No sharp pink blush circles; any cheek warmth is an extremely soft wash blended into the local body color. Each hand has THREE fingers and ONE thumb; a brush or bucket handle can naturally obscure some digits. Use believable grips and connected limbs, not floating hands. Both wear the SAME plain, straight, knee-length cream artist apron, with simple shoulder straps, one small front pocket and restrained green, blue and warm paint marks. No other clothing, accessories or gendered styling.

COURTYARD AND SHARED MURAL
Across all three panels, show a warm, compact community-art courtyard with cream and pale ocher stone walls, a tiled or irregular warm stone floor, and a large wall mural immediately behind the artists. The mural depicts a broad leafy green tree with a branching brown trunk on its left half and a winding blue river passing through low green vegetation to the right. This is clearly PAINTED ON THE WALL, not a real tree growing out of the floor. Preserve the tree's trunk, branch arrangement, river course and wall position as the painted work becomes more complete. A simple low wooden bench and two ordinary paint cans stand at the far left; trailing leaves and small potted flowers flank the mural without cluttering it. The cans carry visible green and blue drips with no printed labels. The right edge has a modest potted flowering plant and hanging greenery. Show enough floor to include complete feet and naturally placed tools. The setting supports the story but must not distract from the characters' changed interaction.

TOP SCENE: SEEKING SOLE RECOGNITION
The GREEN artist stands at the left, fully visible. She holds her own paint-stained brush near her torso in one hand and opens the other arm proudly toward the unfinished mural. Her pleased face and presentation gesture suggest that she wants all the recognition for herself. Above her is a small white thought cloud containing ONE simple gold award cup, with a few short warm emphasis marks and NO text. At floor level, slightly to her right and in front of the mural, a small cream freestanding card has a thin brown border and exactly this readable Persian text: "اثر من". The thought cloud and card belong clearly to green.
The CORAL artist stands at the right with both feet visible, raising her brush to paint leaves or a still incomplete area of the same tree mural. Her other hand holds the handle of an ordinary metal paint bucket. Coral is visibly making a substantial contribution, with a calm small smile, while green is taking the credit. Do not portray coral as crying or as a villain. The tree already has a broad painted form, but parts of the river and vegetation remain unfinished or show pale unpainted wall. No speech bubble appears in this panel.

MIDDLE SCENE: SEEING THE COWORKER'S CONTRIBUTION
Return to the same courtyard during the shared work. The GREEN artist is still at the left, now with her paint-stained brush lowered diagonally across the front of her apron. Her expression is thoughtful and appreciative, and her gaze follows coral's work rather than an imaginary prize. There is no award thought cloud in this scene. The CORAL artist at the right bends forward slightly and paints an important flowing BLUE section of the river with her brush; her free hand holds the blue-dripped paint bucket low at her side. Both are full adults with complete bodies and feet. The mural's tree and foliage are more complete, and coral's visible blue strokes connect the river scene into a coherent whole. Green's lowered brush still shows that she has contributed too. This is equal coworkers making a joint artwork, rather than one teaching a technique to a student. Keep the painterly wall, bench, plants and floor consistent. No new sign, speech, instructional arrow, caption or extra person is needed.

BOTTOM SCENE: DELIBERATELY SHARING AUTHORSHIP
The same tree-and-river mural is now complete, with a gentle light blue sky wash and fuller green vegetation. Green and coral stand close together near the center, both fully visible. Green has one arm warmly around coral's shoulders and opens her other arm outward in an inclusive gesture. Coral smiles with closed friendly arc eyes and holds her paint-stained brush in her free hand. Their equal stance and genuine warmth show the change in green's character. Above them, a single speech bubble belongs to GREEN and reads exactly: "کار هر دومونه!". At the lower left in front of the wall, the same cream authorship card now reads exactly: "اثر ما". Keep it similar in size, shape and location to the original card, with the changed word easy to notice.
At the FAR RIGHT is one ordinary dark camera on a stable three-legged tripod, aimed toward BOTH artists for a shared photograph. Show the camera in an unmistakable side or three-quarter view: its cylindrical lens protrudes LEFTWARD toward the two people, while the side of the camera body is visible. Its optical axis points at the artists, not at the outside edge or the wall behind it. Keep all THREE tripod legs complete and inside the painted floor. There is no photographer, monitor portrait, lens ray or extra character. Keep the bench and blue/green paint cans at the far left. The result is shared recognition and an appreciative human relationship; do not introduce a new trophy, payment, title or reward in the last scene.

TEXT AND FINAL COMPOSITION
The ONLY writing anywhere in the image is the two authorship cards and the final dialogue, using the three exact Persian strings quoted above. Render natural connected Persian letters, readable at book size, in dark hand-lettered marks. No English, numbers, signature, watermark, label, banner or moralizing slogan. Preserve the wide three-row rhythm, clean white gutters, organic watercolor edges, moderate layered washes within the characters and every full foot safely inside its panel. Keep the emotional tone warm and gently witty: an artist initially presenting a shared work as her own finally recognizes and includes the person who helped make it.

COMPOSITION

Each is viewed from the front at a slight elevated angle that shows the tabletop and the standing friends' full bodies and both feet below it. Keep the complete wooden worktable, its legs, every foot and all important props INSIDE each scene. Leave clean white paper around the full image with softly irregular watercolor scene endings. CHARACTER SYSTEM
Three distinct adult friends across the two scenes: GREEN is the continuing central character on the LEFT in both scenes. In the upper scene green is a YOUNG ADULT and the friend on the RIGHT is an OLDER BLUE ADULT. In the lower scene the SAME green person is now an OLDER ADULT, while the friend on the RIGHT is a YOUNG PINK ADULT. All are equally capable friends with comparable adult stature, not parent/child, nurse/patient or teacher/pupil.
All have simple medium, balanced neutral adult bodies, moderate arms and legs and near-parallel torso sides. Never chibi, childlike, very thin or bulky. No breasts, pinched waist, protruding hips or buttocks, waist indentations or gendered body shape. No hair, ears, noses or necks. Heads are true PERFECT CIRCLES, width equal to height, with no oval shape, jaw, chin or flattened bottom. Each head joins shoulders directly, distinguished by a soft crescent contact shadow in a darker shade of the local body color.
Every friend wears the SAME plain straight CREAM apron with simple shoulder straps and an unwaisted bib/skirt; no other clothing, no shoes. Apron hems are visible below the tabletop. The body's own color continues down the two legs into simple rounded feet, with physically continuous torso-to-leg alignment. Each complete hand has THREE fingers plus ONE thumb; use natural dough/cutter grips with normal overlap and no extra digits.
Eyes use the book's minimal friendly design: small dark oval eyes where open, optionally a tiny glint INSIDE the dark eye; absolutely no surrounding white sclera. Smiling closed eyes are small upward arcs. Only the young pink friend has a few SHORT fine upper-outer eyelashes, added to the SAME modest eye shape and size. No huge lashes or doll eyes. No lashes on green or blue. In the upper scene BOTH friends have cheerful closed arc eyes and open smiling mouths. Older blue wears simple round clear-lens, warm brown-rimmed glasses, plus TWO OR THREE fine short dark-local-blue crow's-feet strokes near the outer eye. In the lower scene older green wears similar round clear glasses, cheerful closed arc eyes and TWO OR THREE fine short dark-local-green wrinkles beside the outer eye. Do not turn glasses into opaque eye whites. Young pink has friendly open dark oval eyes with tiny internal glints, short lashes and an open delighted smile. On the flour-dusted tabletop: at LEFT is one cream ceramic bowl with a blue horizontal band containing bread dough; near center is a small oval dough portion. At RIGHT is one complete shallow dark-gray-rimmed rectangular baking tray with a small pretzel-shaped piece and an oval dough portion. The heading "سال‌ها بعد" is at upper-left. Green remains on the LEFT with exactly the same green identity, circular head and balanced body, now with round glasses and a few subtle eye wrinkles. The YOUNG ADULT pink friend is on the RIGHT in the identical straight cream apron. They are delightedly inventing playful bread shapes together. Green uses both hands to finish a small pale golden RABBIT-shaped dough loaf in front of him; its simple long ears, small body and one tiny dark dough-eye make the rabbit shape recognizable. Pink lifts a small silver STAR-shaped cutter near the chest with the hand at image-right; the other hand rests naturally beside the dough on the table. Pink's eyes and smile face the shared activity. Add a few restrained joy/emphasis marks near the friends and star cutter, without words.
